# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md; ranking and track confirmed in your partner's words, 2026-11-10. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace of four packages (root `pyproject.toml`). Azure platform per the ADR, whose status is Proposed (2026-10-05); acceptance is a Stage 7 `Consumes`.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index baseline from archived quarterly indexes over a chosen quarter range | R1; §2.1, §4.2 | A | 1 | About 2 SEC requests per quarter (listing + index); bytes and time per quarter measured by Stage 1; range not yet set (§4.8) |
| O2 | Daily indexes ingested on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | R2; §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year, 1–2 requests each; seconds at 3 req/s (§4.8) |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet, parsed and validated from those indexes | R3; §4.4, §4.5, §4.6 | A | 3 | Measured by Stage 1 (rows, elapsed time, peak memory per quarter) |

| O6 | Original index bytes kept, so a parser change re-runs without re-downloading | R6; §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage ≈ raw bytes per retained snapshot; per-quarter bytes measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Periodic re-checks of quarterly indexes that pick up later SEC corrections | R7; §4.2, §4.4 | A | 7 | Weekly re-download of every supported quarter, about 2 requests each (§4.8) |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter, end to end
      Objective: Fetch one real archived quarterly master index from the SEC, parse it, and write its rows locally as Parquet in the §4.5 row contract.
      Outcomes: O1, O3 (one quarter)
      Consumes: the generated scaffolds only; an SEC User-Agent identity from your partner (§4.8 `sec.user_agent`)
      Produces: a downloader and master-index parser for the chosen quarter's format; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one named archived quarter is downloaded with an identifying User-Agent at no more than 3 req/s; O3 — its rows are written as `sec-index-v1` Parquet, the row count matches the index's data lines, and a malformed row fails the run instead of being dropped; the findings file records bytes, request count, elapsed time and peak memory of the real run
      Leaves out: raw retention and replay (Stage 2); range enumeration, daily indexes, discovery, checkpoints, typed configuration and legacy-format fixtures (Stage 3); key identity, precedence, generations and manifests (Stage 4); reconciliation and the withdrawal gate (Stage 5); the shared request budget (Stage 6); Azure deployment (Stage 7); scheduling, alerts and runbooks (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Raw snapshots and replay
      Objective: Keep each accepted index's original bytes content-addressed with its snapshot record, and transform from storage without SEC requests.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader and parser
      Produces: a local content-addressed raw store, snapshot and processing records, quarantine, and observation output keyed by snapshot, parser and schema version
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observations from stored bytes with zero SEC requests, and an HTML or truncated body is quarantined, never accepted as an index
      Leaves out: ADLS and Table Storage backing (Stage 7); the published state (Stage 4)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Backfill range and daily ingestion
      Objective: One discover-collect-transform path that ingests a configured quarterly range and daily indexes, with source-file checkpoints and catch-up.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O5, O11
      Consumes: Stage 2 raw store and processing records
      Produces: the `discover`, `collect` and `transform` commands; immutable worksets; source and attempt records; validated configuration (§4.8 keys); golden fixtures for the supported range
      Exit: O1 — a backfill over a configured range reports complete, pending and failed sources separately; O2 — a daily run catches up across a multi-quarter outage, reports `no_new_sources` on an empty listing, and a failed listing does not advance the boundary; O5 — backfill and daily runs go through the same downloader, parser and transform code; O11 — invalid configuration is refused before any network request
      Leaves out: publication (Stage 4); reconciliation (Stage 5); the shared request budget (Stage 6); ADF schedules (Stage 7, Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Quarter generations and the active pointer
      Objective: Resolve observations into a canonical catalog and publish each quarter as a complete generation behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O3, O9
      Consumes: Stage 2 observation output; Stage 3 transform results
      Produces: the `publish` command, generation manifests, change reports and a locally backed conditional pointer
      Exit: O3 — repeated inputs produce the same logical catalog with unique keys and amendments kept distinct; O9 — under crash injection before files finish, before the pointer update and after it, readers see only complete generations, and a competing publisher cannot overwrite a newer pointer
      Leaves out: the withdrawal gate (Stage 5); Table Storage conditional writes (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation and the withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and hold any key removal for hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4 publication and change reports
      Produces: the reconciliation workflow and approval records
      Exit: O7 — a re-read records additions and field updates, and unchanged hashes with unchanged versions skip transformation; O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its source hash and candidate generation, open-quarter absence and response failures withdraw nothing, and a stale daily replay cannot bring back a withdrawn key
      Leaves out: weekly scheduling (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: One SEC request budget
      Objective: Put every collector's SEC requests, retries included, under one lease-coordinated budget.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 3 collectors; Stage 5 reconciliation collector
      Produces: lease-based collector coordination and the access-blocked halt
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors never issue requests at the same time, retries count against the budget, lease loss stops new requests, and a 403 halts SEC access for the run
      Leaves out: lease behavior on deployed Azure Storage (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure platform and smoke test
      Objective: Deploy pipelines, jobs, storage and monitoring to an isolated Azure environment with triggers disabled, and pass the integration tests and a bounded live smoke test.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: the ADR and spec accepted, with range, handoff date, SEC identity and environment settings recorded (§7 step 1); Stages 2–6
      Produces: infrastructure under version control, a pinned image digest, ADLS and Table Storage backings, and log delivery
      Exit: O4 — in the isolated environment, ADF starts and polls a job to a terminal outcome and requires its result file, an ambiguous start does not relaunch, the smoke test of one archived quarter and one daily index records byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate, and replay from raw storage with SEC access disabled gives unchanged output
      Leaves out: trigger enablement, production backfill, alert recipients and runbooks (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Production baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill and daily catch-up, enable the schedules, and exercise the runbooks, alerts and rollback.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7
      Consumes: Stage 7 deployment and smoke-test results
      Produces: a release record naming image and configuration versions and active quarter generations; runbooks (§8)
      Exit: O1 — every requested baseline unit is published, or an approved incomplete range is recorded; O2 — daily ingestion is caught up from the handoff date, its trigger is enabled, and the next scheduled runs match their durable reports; O7 — one manual reconciliation runs with gated candidates resolved, then its weekly trigger is enabled; alerts, runbooks and rollback have been exercised
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans
